findings.body: datetime.datetime.utcnow() is deprecated since Python 3.12 and returns a naive datetime.
findings.failure_scenario: When this value is compared with a timezone-aware datetime, Python raises TypeError instead of completing the comparison.
findings.title: Use timezone-aware datetime.now()

findings.body: The function sorts the entire list to find the last element, which is O(N log N), contradicting the docstring's claim of constant time.
findings.failure_scenario: When processing large lists of records, this function becomes a bottleneck, causing unnecessary CPU usage and latency.
findings.suggestion: return str(records[-1].get("id")) if records else None
findings.title: Inefficient sorting for newest record lookup

findings.body: Accessing row["total"] without checking for existence will raise a KeyError if the dictionary is missing the key.
findings.failure_scenario: When a row in rows lacks a "total" key, the function crashes with a KeyError instead of gracefully handling the missing data.
findings.title: Missing key validation for 'total'

findings.body: datetime.datetime.utcnow() is deprecated since Python 3.12 and returns a naive datetime.
findings.failure_scenario: When this value is compared with a timezone-aware datetime, Python raises TypeError instead of completing the comparison.
findings.title: Use timezone-aware datetime.now()

findings.anchor: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] = []) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.body: The function uses a mutable list as a default argument. The list is created once when the function is defined and persists across all calls, causing the function to accumulate data indefinitely and leak memory.
findings.failure_scenario: When the function is called repeatedly with different event types, the events list grows without bound, consuming increasing memory and eventually causing a MemoryError or performance degradation.
findings.suggestion: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.title: Use immutable default argument to prevent unbounded growth

findings.body: The function checks 'if label in seen' on a list, resulting in O(N) lookups per iteration. For large inputs, this degrades to O(N^2) time complexity.
findings.failure_scenario: When processing a large batch of payment labels, the function performs increasingly slow linear searches, causing significant latency and CPU saturation.
findings.title: Use a set for O(1) lookups in unique_payment_labels

findings.anchor: query = f"SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '{owner_id}'"
findings.body: The owner_id is directly interpolated into the SQL query string, allowing an attacker to inject malicious SQL. Use a parameterized query instead.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker provides a customer_id containing SQL injection payload (e.g., '1' OR '1'='1') which is executed as part of the query, potentially revealing or modifying all order rows for any customer.
findings.suggestion:
query = "SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = %s"
    cursor.execute(query, (owner_id,))
findings.title: Use parameterized query to prevent SQL injection

findings.anchor: """Return the newest queue identifier in constant time.
findings.body: The function sorts records, which is O(n log n), but the docstring claims it returns the newest identifier in constant time. This is misleading and incorrect.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer relying on the constant-time claim may implement inefficient algorithms elsewhere, leading to performance issues.
findings.title: Remove misleading constant-time claim

findings.body: The function sorts all records to find the newest, which is O(n log n). Since records are assumed to arrive in chronological order, the newest is simply the last element, which is O(1).
findings.failure_scenario: For large datasets, the sorting operation becomes a performance bottleneck, especially when called frequently.
findings.title: Replace sorting with last element lookup

findings.failure_scenario: When this timestamp is compared with a timezone-aware datetime, Python raises a TypeError instead of completing the comparison.
findings.title: Use timezone-aware datetime.now() instead of utcnow()
